tasks.whyItMatters: Troubleshooting questions on SAA-C03 often require identifying the narrowest broken layer. A bad ALB health-check path produces an unhealthy target; an ALB security-group problem blocks clients; a web-group source problem blocks ALB-to-EC2 traffic; an RDS-group rule problem blocks EC2-to-RDS traffic. Incorrect MySQL credentials and an incorrect DNS endpoint are different failures from security-group blocks.

tasks.whyItMatters: CloudWatch helps identify resource saturation and availability symptoms. RDS automated backups support point-in-time recovery within retention, while manual snapshots are retained until deleted. SAA-C03 questions mentioning recovery point objectives, point-in-time recovery, retained backups, or a user-initiated recovery copy should make you distinguish automated backups from manual snapshots.

programme.subtitle: Build and validate a three-tier SAA-C03 practice architecture: internet → Application Load Balancer → EC2 → private RDS for MySQL.
programme.description: In Europe (London) (eu-west-2), use an existing VPC that has subnets in at least two Availability Zones. Create separate security groups for an internet-facing Application Load Balancer, EC2 web targets, and a private RDS for MySQL DB instance. Deploy a simple HTTP workload behind the ALB, validate target health and traffic distribution, then verify the private EC2-to-RDS network path.
programme.displayName: RDS, EC2, and Application Load Balancer Follow Along
programme.learningOutcome: Build, verify, monitor, troubleshoot, and manually clean up an internet-facing Application Load Balancer that forwards HTTP traffic to EC2 targets while a private RDS for MySQL DB instance accepts port 3306 traffic only from the EC2 security group. Recognize SAA-C03 scenarios that call for ALB, security-group references, private database placement, Multi-AZ deployments, read replicas, and Auto Scaling.
